title: Momentum and collisions — independent questions-only review
author: chatgpt-0378a7b6b7c2/la7
assumptions: Idealized classical one-dimensional carts with fixed strictly positive masses; right is positive.

Cart A begins strictly to the left of B with a positive gap. Before contact velocities are constant. A future encounter requires uA > uB; equal or receding velocities must not be presented as a collision event.
For computed collision endpoints, the two-cart system has zero net external impulse. Perfectly elastic and completely inelastic (stick-together) are explicitly selected model assumptions.

Only endpoint translational velocities, signed momentum and translational kinetic energy are modeled. No impact force, duration, deformation path, friction, rotation, material property, measurement or learning-effectiveness claim.
Every question is self-contained because the existing learner can select questions in a different order.
The external-impulse question explicitly departs from the zero-impulse assumption to test that boundary.

questions.prompt: Cart A has mass 2 kg and velocity -3 m/s, where right is positive. What is its signed momentum?
A 1 kg cart moves at +4 m/s and a 2 kg cart moves at -2 m/s. What are their total signed momentum p and total translational kinetic energy K?
Treat both carts together as one fixed-mass system. The net external impulse during their interaction is zero. Which statement must hold?
options: Each cart keeps its individual momentum.
The sum of the carts' signed momenta is unchanged.
The sum of their translational kinetic energies is unchanged.
Both carts must be stationary afterward.

questions.prompt: Cart A (2 kg, +3 m/s) approaches cart B (1 kg, 0 m/s) from the left. They undergo a completely inelastic collision with zero net external impulse. What common velocity do they have afterward?

Cart A (2 kg, +3 m/s) approaches cart B (1 kg, 0 m/s) from the left. An ideal elastic collision conserves momentum and translational kinetic energy, and the carts separate afterward. Which pair of final velocities (vA, vB) is consistent with this event?
Two 1 kg carts approach each other: A, initially on the left, has uA = +4 m/s; B has uB = -2 m/s. After an ideal one-dimensional elastic collision, what are (vA, vB)?

Cart A (2 kg, +3 m/s) meets cart B (1 kg, 0 m/s). They stick and move together at +2 m/s with no net external impulse. How much translational kinetic energy is converted to other forms during this idealized event?
Two 1 kg carts approach at +3 m/s and -3 m/s. They stick and stop, reducing their total translational kinetic energy from 9 J to 0 J. Which interpretation is justified?
options: The 9 J of energy has been destroyed.
Momentum conservation has failed because the carts stopped.
The 9 J has changed into other energy forms; this endpoint model does not resolve their distribution.
Exactly 9 J must have become sound, with no other energy change.

questions.prompt: A begins to the left of B with a positive gap. Both keep their incoming velocities until contact. Which pair (uA, uB) makes the gap shrink so a future encounter is possible?
A begins to the left of B with a positive gap. Both move at +2 m/s and have no acceleration before contact. What should a collision explorer report?
options: Their gap stays constant, so these inputs do not produce a future collision.
They must immediately stick because their velocities are equal.
They undergo an elastic collision that exchanges their masses.
A collision occurs after one second for every positive gap.

questions.prompt: The two-cart system initially has total momentum +6 kg m/s. During an interaction it receives a known net external impulse of +2 kg m/s. What follows?
options: Its final momentum is +6 kg m/s because internal forces cancel.
Its final momentum is +4 kg m/s.
Its final momentum is +8 kg m/s; the zero-external-impulse collision formulas do not apply unchanged.
No final total momentum can be inferred even though the net impulse is given.

questions.prompt: For two fixed positive masses and a fixed total momentum, why is the shared velocity of a completely inelastic endpoint the state with the least translational kinetic energy?
options: Any relative motion adds nonnegative kinetic energy above the center-of-mass motion, and this extra term is zero only at a shared velocity.
A shared velocity always means both carts have zero velocity.
Momentum conservation permits only one possible pair of final velocities.
Kinetic energy is signed, so positive and negative contributions cancel at a shared velocity.
